nodeData.note: The whole system: levels, competencies, values, assessment.

children.note: Kenya's Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) is the school system from nursery to Grade 12. It aims for children who can use what they learn, not only remember it. This map shows the big picture: the levels, the skills and values, assessment, and the part parents play.

nodeData.note: Kenya's Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) is the school system from nursery to Grade 12. It aims for children who can use what they learn, not only remember it. This map shows the big picture: the levels, the skills and values, assessment, and the part parents play.

children.note: In plain words: school should help children DO things with what they learn. Knowing facts still matters, but using them is the goal.

children.topic: Able to use what you learn
children.note: KICD describes a competency as being able to use the right knowledge, skills, attitudes and values to do a task well. Example: measuring and pricing items at the market, not just reciting a times table.

manas.q: What is a competency, in plain words?

children.note: Lessons are meant to be hands-on: experiments, projects, group work and real tasks, so children learn through experience.
The framework puts the child, their needs, talents and interests at the heart of learning, rather than the syllabus alone.
Teachers plan learning activities that suit each child, then guide and observe, instead of only lecturing.
CBC was launched in 2017 and phased in grade by grade. You may also hear it called CBE (Competency Based Education).

manas.q: In which year was CBC launched in Kenya?

children.note: 8-4-4 was the system CBC is replacing. Here is a neutral side-by-side of the main ideas, not a judgement of either.
Eight years of primary, four of secondary and four of university, introduced in 1985.

children.note: The 2019 framework notes concerns that 8-4-4 was heavy on content and exams, with limited practical skills.
CBC aims to cover less content in depth and focus on applying knowledge in real life.
8-4-4 relied mostly on final exams. CBC aims to balance ongoing classroom checks with end-of-level assessments.
CBC has 2 years pre-primary, 6 primary, 3 junior school and 3 senior school before college or university.

children.note: Seven big skills every learner builds in every learning area, from PP1 to Grade 12. One bubble each, with an everyday example.
Speaking, listening, writing and working well with others. Example: siblings planning together how to share the chores.

manas.q: Name the core competency about talking and working with others.

children.note: Believing in yourself and your ability to manage tasks. Example: a child who tries again after a sum goes wrong, and gets it right.
Thinking things through and finding solutions. Example: working out why the tomato seedlings are wilting and what to change.

manas.q: Which core competency is about reasoning and finding solutions?

children.note: Making new things and ideas. Example: building a toy lorry from a carton and bottle tops.
Caring for your community and country. Example: helping clean the estate or school compound.
Using phones, computers and the internet safely and well. Example: looking up the weather with a parent and talking about safe use.

manas.q: Which core competency covers using technology safely?

children.note: Knowing how to keep learning on your own. Example: a child who looks up a new word, notes it and uses it later.
Values CBC aims to nurture, drawn from Kenya's Constitution (2019 framework). Parents are the first teachers of values; children learn them mostly by example.
Doing your part. Example: feeding the chickens every morning without being reminded.
Treating people and things well. Example: greeting elders and waiting your turn to speak.
Doing your best work. Example: rewriting homework neatly because you care about it.
Helping others who are in need. Example: checking on a sick neighbour or a classmate who is sad.
Accepting people who differ from us. Example: making friends with a classmate from another community or faith.
Telling the truth and keeping promises. Example: returning extra change to the shopkeeper.

manas.q: Name a CBC value about telling the truth.

children.note: Being someone others can rely on, and trusting others fairly. Example: a child trusted to carry the family's shopping money.
Choosing what is right even when no one is watching. Example: not copying a friend's work in class.
KICD has values-based education materials and reported plans for a nationwide rollout by 2026. Ask your school how it is used.

children.note: Pre-primary is the start of school under the Competency Based Curriculum. It is the gentle first step into learning with other children.
Pre-primary has two years. PP1 comes first, then PP2, then the child moves to Grade 1.

manas.q: What are the two years of pre-primary called?

manas.q: Which grade comes straight after PP2?

children.note: Children listen to stories, follow simple instructions, answer questions and share their own news.

children.note: The top stage of basic education under CBC, after junior school.
Senior school lasts three years: Grade 10, Grade 11 and Grade 12.

manas.q: Which grades make up senior school?

children.note: The 2019 curriculum framework places senior school learners at about 16 to 18 years old. Some learners will be younger or older.

manas.q: What ages does the 2019 framework give for senior school?

children.note: Learners move up from junior school after Grade 9. Grade 10 under CBC started in 2026.
Unlike earlier levels, each learner follows one pathway that matches their interests, strengths and hoped-for careers.

manas.q: What is a pathway in senior school?

children.topic: A track is a group of subjects
children.note: Inside each pathway are tracks. A track is a combination of related subjects, for example Pure Sciences inside STEM.

manas.q: What is a track in senior school?

children.note: The three pathways are STEM, Social Sciences, and Arts and Sports Science.

manas.q: Name the three senior school pathways.

children.note: Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics. For learners who enjoy numbers, experiments, machines, computers and farming.
Science and maths studied in depth, the base for medicine, engineering and research. Subjects: Core Mathematics, Essential Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, General Science.

manas.q: Which STEM track includes Biology, Chemistry and Physics?

children.note: Science used in daily life: growing food, computers and running a healthy home. Subjects: Agriculture, Computer Studies, Home Science, Information Communication Technology.

manas.q: Which STEM track includes Agriculture and Computer Studies?

children.note: Hands-on skills for building, fixing and making things. Subjects: Aviation, Building Construction, Electricity, Metal Work, Power Mechanics, Woodwork, Media Technology, Marine & Fisheries.

manas.q: Name two subjects in the Technical Studies track.

children.note: The course book lists show both Core Mathematics and Essential Mathematics. Ask your school which one fits your child's track.

manas.q: What two kinds of mathematics appear in the STEM course lists?

children.note: For learners who enjoy languages, reading, people, history, places, faith and business.
Reading, writing, speaking and enjoying stories in Kenyan and foreign languages. Subjects: English, Literature in English, Kiswahili, Fasihi ya Kiswahili, Arabic, French, German (Grade 11 list only).

manas.q: Which Social Sciences track includes Literature in English and Fasihi ya Kiswahili?

children.note: How people live, believe, govern, trade and look after places. Subjects: Christian Religious Education (CRE), Islamic Religious Education (IRE), Community Service Learning, History & Citizenship, Geography, Business Studies, Life Skills (Grade 11 list only).

manas.q: Which track includes History & Citizenship, Geography and Business Studies?

children.note: For learners with talent and love for music, drama, art, sport and fitness.
Creating and performing: songs, dance, plays, films and visual art. Subjects: Music and Dance, Theatre and Film, Fine Arts.

manas.q: Name the three subjects in the Arts track.

children.note: How the body moves, trains and stays healthy, plus playing and organising sport. Subjects: Sports and Recreation, Physical Education.

manas.q: Which two subjects make up the Sports Science track?

children.note: The 2019 framework used older wording, including a talent pathway for drama, music and dance. Today's lists call it Arts and Sports Science.
